sq-glb-title: the same wave on a globe

fx-rl-alt: Left: stations scattered around an unknown centre, each with the time its wave arrived; circles of equal arrival time grow around the centre. Right: the arrival times against each station's distance from a trial centre: at the right centre they fall on one smooth curve, at a wrong one they scatter. The same is done with distances on the globe and with distances on the flat map, each allowed its own curve
fx-rl-1: the centre is unknown: it is fitted
rl-res-x-n: distance from each model's centre (°); beyond ±40 s: at the edge
sh-map-best: the best map for one ring ({c})
sh-read-globe: Globe, 103° (nothing fitted): {b} of {n} stations on the wrong side

sh-read-common: one ring for the nine on this map (ρ = {r}°): {b} of {n} wrong
sh-read-own-none: this map, this quake: no ring does better than none, {b}
sh-read-common-none: one ring for the nine on this map: none does better than no ring, {b} of {n} wrong
sq-cv-schem: ray paths schematic, radii to scale
rb-read-g: globe: {a} s (one curve for all), {b} s (a curve each)
rb-read-f: best flat map: {a} s, {b} s · North Pole map: {c} s, {d} s
rb-h-x: observed − fitted P time (s), one curve for every earthquake
rb-h-note: beyond ±40 s: not drawn ({p} % of the North Pole map's)
rb-d-flat: best flat map ({c}): distance on the disc
rb-d-x: distance from each model's centre (degrees); darker: more stations
rb-q-x: globe's scatter for this earthquake (s), one curve for all
rb-q-t: one dot per earthquake: the globe does better for {w} of {n}
rb-q-t2: the globe does better for {w} of {n}
rb-q-leg: ● black: the named earthquakes · log scales
rb-s-f: best flat map for one ring ({c}): distance on the disc
rb-s-x: distance from the epicentre; bar height: % of stations with a direct P; paler: fewer stations
rb-sr-g: globe, 103° (no fit): {a} wrong · one ring for all ({r}°): {b}
rb-sr-f: best flat map, one ring: {a} wrong · North Pole map: {p} · one ring per earthquake: {o}
rb-r-alt: Box plots of the Earth's radius from every Rayleigh-wave arrival of {q} large shallow earthquakes, with and without the ocean/continent correction, and of the per-earthquake medians
fx-rc-alt: Arrival time against distance for three earthquakes: three copies of the same curve, shifted up or down by each earthquake's own origin time, with each earthquake's stations on its own copy. Only the shift and the centre belong to each earthquake; the shape is one for all
fx-rc-1: distance from each earthquake's own centre
sr-schem: real data throughout; globes in true proportion
sr-wave-a: An earthquake is one tick heard by hundreds of clocks.
sr-wave-b: Each station writes down when the wave arrived. We keep only that time, and the station's latitude and longitude.
sr-centre-a: We find each earthquake's centre ourselves.
sr-centre-b: It is the point from which the times fall on one curve. No catalogue, no radius, and every flat map gets the same freedom.
sr-law-a: {{n}} earthquakes, {{st}} stations, one curve for all.
sr-law-b: Real clocks miss the globe's curve by {{g}} s. On the best flat map they miss by {{b}} s.
sr-quakes-a: Earthquake by earthquake, the same verdict.
sr-quakes-b: The globe does better for {{w}} of the {{n}}. Each dot above the line is one earthquake the flat map gets worse.
sr-maps-a: The flat model may choose where its map is centred.
sr-maps-b: Of {{nscan}} centres tried, the best still misses {{xr}} times as much as the globe.
sr-shadow-a: Beyond one angle, the direct wave never arrives.
sr-shadow-b: {{sn}} stations: on the globe the edge is sharp, the same for every earthquake. On a flat map it smears.
sr-size-a: Surface waves give the size of the Earth.
sr-size-b: {{rn}} arrivals of {{rq}} earthquakes: median {{rm}} km, against 6,371 km.
sr-end-a: Same clocks, same freedom, two shapes.
sr-end-b: Only the sphere makes the arrival times agree.
sr-darker: darker: the flat map misses more
sr-alt: Animation: the P wave of the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake lighting real stations on a globe; a trial centre sliding until the arrival times fall on one curve; the residuals of every large shallow earthquake under one curve, narrow for the globe and wide for the best flat map; one dot per earthquake above the line of equality; a map of every flat-map centre tried; the share of stations with a direct P wave against distance; the radius from every surface-wave arrival; a summary
wv-read-p: {s}: the P wave came from {b}° (measured from its motion)
wv-read-f: straight line on the North Pole map: {f}°
wv-r: R radial, away from the source
wv-x: minutes after the P onset at this station
wv-clip: traces clipped at 1/{c} of the peak, to show the early waves
wv-plane-rt: R across, T up (seen from above)
wv-d-x: measured direction of the P wave minus the predicted direction of the epicentre
fx-pol-alt: Three small boxes showing the path of the ground during a few seconds: a straight line tilted near the vertical for a P wave, a straight horizontal line across the path for an S or Love wave, and an ellipse in the vertical plane for a Rayleigh wave; under each, its rectilinearity L, close to 1 for the lines and small for the ellipse
fx-pol-4: λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ λ₃: the spread of the motion along its three main directions
sr-kinds-a: Each kind of wave moves the ground its own way.
sr-kinds-b: Three components tell them apart with no travel-time table: P along the ray, S and Love across it, Rayleigh rolling on an ellipse.
msr-schem: real P times only · colour = the station's real latitude, never read by the fit
msr-naive-a: Each time becomes a straight-line distance.
msr-naive-b: {{n}} P readings, no coordinate: one unit = 100 s of travel. First, everything is forced onto a plane, two numbers per station.
msr-plane-b: Positions, origin times and the speed law all move until the times fit. It stalls at {{ps}} s.
msr-lift-a: Same start, one number more per station.
msr-lift-b: Let free in the third dimension, the stations settle at {{ss}} s: {{ratio}} times better than the plane.
msr-arcs-a: The cloud is hollow: it is a sphere.
msr-arcs-b: Every station within {{rel}} of one radius. Only now the straight lines are drawn as arcs on it.
msr-speed-a: The speed comes from globe distances.
msr-speed-b: So change it by ±25 %. The size follows, R = {{kmv}} × v₀ km; the shape does not move.
msr-laws-a: Another speed law still gives a sphere.
msr-laws-b: Curvature shifted, or one constant speed: the radius runs from {{rmin}} to {{rmax}} units and the fit worsens, but the cloud stays round.
msr-map-b: Turned to fit best (rotation only), the stations sit {{vs}} rms from their published positions. Red dashes: each station's error, too small to see until we zoom in.
msr-v0: speed at the start of the law
msr-quakes: × = the 8 earthquakes that read the most stations
msr-alt: Animation: stations placed from earthquake P times alone; first as straight-line distances on a plane, which stalls; then from the same start in space, where they settle on a sphere; the lines then drawn as great-circle arcs; the speed of propagation changed, which only changes the size; other speed laws, which keep a sphere; finally the cloud turned onto the real map, with a red dashed arc from each station to its published position
